page_placements.theme: Abliteration beyond refusal: off-target behaviour, capability retention and output drift, by model and tool

record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports harmful-refusal rates after a representation-editing/abliteration weight edit across models, testing practical refusal removal with a method different from the original single-direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports a benchmark table for ICONOCLAST and HERETIC. The direction methods, layer selections, and blending strategies are described as workflow options, but results used only to choose parameters are not recorded as findings. No results test adding a direction or the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.test_reason: A tool repository that applies abliteration and reports only its own method against the HERETIC tool. It gives post-edit harmful-refusal counts, but no refusal rate for the unedited models, so it cannot show how much refusal the edit removes. Its numbers measure one tool against another, not whether V2 holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly correct. The README claims ICONOCLAST beats HERETIC on all 10 models. Its own table shows harmful refusals lower in only 6 of 10 (tied in 4) and KL lower in only 8 of 10; Falcon3 KL is 6.14 vs 0.16. It also claims lower KL means capabilities are retained, which is untested.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes per-layer contrastive refusal directions, benign-subspace preservation, and Optuna optimization, rather than the original single-direction intervention. This is a tool repository that reports benchmark results; it does not claim to reproduce the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says its research workflow searches direction methods, layer selections, and blending strategies; it does not report how those choices change the benchmark outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-edit harmful-refusal counts out of 20 for ICONOCLAST against HERETIC on 10 models. ICONOCLAST is lower on 6 and tied on 4. Qwen3.5-9B base is 10/20 under both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration tools differ in residual harmful-refusal rate after editing, by model.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign overrefusal counts out of 64 for each tool after editing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration tools differ in benign overrefusal after editing.

fits_no_version.finding: KL divergence from the base model: ICONOCLAST is lower in 8 of 10 and higher for Falcon3 (6.14 vs 0.16) and Yi.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-subspace preservation lowers KL cost of abliteration in most but not all models.

record.problems: Evidence is README-reported benchmark data only. The README does not state the refusal-evaluation protocol, prompt contents, uncertainty, or exact edits used for the benchmark. It calls KL a utility metric, but this is not a direct general-capability evaluation. Qwen3.5-9B base is included alongside instruct/chat models.
record.rows_left_out: None; all 60 rows are the reported refusal, benign-overrefusal, and KL results for the 10 models and two methods.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of a difference-in-means direction against an unedited control.
No pre-edit refusal rates, so the amount of refusal removed is not shown. No capability benchmarks, only KL divergence.
Per-layer directions are used, but single and multiple directions are not compared.

missing.what: Refusal rates of the unedited models, needed to read any row as a removal effect.
missing.locator: Not in README; may be in PUBLISHABLE_RESULTS.md, TECHNICAL_NOTE.md or final_report_acl.tex (unread).

missing.what: Repository report files may contain fuller results, such as direction-method comparisons or nullspace runs.

record.verdict_notes: I reclassify the record from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. This is a tool README comparing two abliteration tools, and it has no unedited baseline. The record's V2 verdicts are dropped. The prompt sets are small (20 harmful, 64 benign) and no uncertainty is given.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test of the original difference-in-means direction, its removal or addition, or preservation of other abilities under that intervention.
The README reports refusal results after weight editing, but does not state whether the evaluated edited checkpoints were released or provide details of the editing procedure and evaluation protocol.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No result comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages for whether a removable direction exists.
